summary: Iteration 12 — Multi-unit tool listings + location state filter. 11/11 backend pytest tests pass and full frontend E2E flow (login → multi-unit tool → date range → qty=2 → request booking → /bookings/:id with quantity badge) succeeds with correct linear pricing.
critical_code_review_comments: _booked_qty_by_date / _max_booked_qty_in_range correctly count pending+approved; declined/cancelled bookings free stock back — verified by sequential booking test.
create_booking and update_booking_status/approve both call peak-day check — defends against race on approve. Approve excludes self via exclude_booking_id — correct.

GET /api/tools/{id}/unavailable_dates has a 365-day horizon — long-tail bookings beyond a year aren't shown in calendar. Acceptable for rental UX, but worth a comment for future devs. (Tests adjusted to use dates within 365 days.)

ToolDetail quantity-selector is rendered even before a date range is selected (test observed it visible pre-date). Spec said 'after picking a date range' — minor UX divergence, not a regression. Worth confirming with PM.
ipapi.co geolocation fetch is blocked by CORS in sandbox — silent fallback to USD works (pre-existing, see iter11 notes). Not a regression.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all assertions passed in single E2E run)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Pressure Washer 2000 PSI tool_id observed = tool_2b87967933dd (Mississauga, owned by Diego, quantity_total=5). The /api/tools state filter uses case-insensitive PREFIX match (regex ^state) on location.state. Backend treats missing quantity_total as 1 (no crash). The unavailable_dates endpoint has a 365-day horizon. Frontend ToolDetail renders quantity-selector even before a date range is chosen; quantity_value defaults to 1 and increments to N (1..quantity_total). booking-quantity-badge appears as '× N units' when booking.quantity > 1.
rca of the issue: No bugs found. One observation: spec says quantity-selector should appear AFTER date range is picked, but currently it renders unconditionally on multi-unit tool detail page. Functionally harmless because the booking endpoint validates qty vs. range stock server-side.
